report.summary: Two of three ships are clean; one needs a light framing fix. Action item: on the "a-skill-not-a-bigger-model" ship, tighten the headline/framing — claim-accuracy flagged (minor) that "a skill, not a bigger model" and "a free local model" understate that the method DID use frontier models at authoring time (Actor = Gemini-2.5-Pro wrote the skill, ceiling = Gemini-2.5-Flash), so the "cost goes to zero" claim holds for runtime inference only, not skill production; a secondary caveat is the generalisation resting on just 8 held-out records. Notably, that same ship's dedicated caveat section was rated exemplary by the honest-caveats reviewer, so the fix is confined to the headline claim, not the disclosures. All three ships fully reconcile on numbers, carry honest and unsoftened caveats, and have every link/asset/hero image resolving 200.

issues.issue: Framing/claim tension (numbers themselves reconcile exactly). The headline 'a skill, not a bigger model' and 'a free local model' understate that the method DID require a bigger model at authoring time: result.json shows the skill Actor is frontier Gemini-2.5-Pro and the 1.000 ceiling is Gemini-2.5-Flash, with Qwen2.5:7B as the local Executor (0.938 -> 1.000). The 'cost goes to zero' claim therefore holds only for runtime inference, not for skill production, which the headline elides. Secondary caveat: the 'perfect 1.000 on records it had never seen' generalisation rests on only 8 held-out records. Note: the honest-caveats reviewer rated this ship's dedicated 'What's still off' section exemplary (small gap front-loaded into opening and subtitle), so the fix is limited to the headline claim, not the disclosures.

findings.issue: Caveat present, specific, and unsoftened. The real limitation is stated plainly in a marked 'What's still off' section and is not dressed up.
findings.evidence: 'It alerts, it does not enforce, and that separation is deliberate: cutting off a call mid-flight can break real work'; 'It can only see what gets logged, so an agent that calls a model without recording the cost is invisible to it'; and an unusually candid self-bug disclosure — the original 'silently capped at a thousand rows... and would have quietly hidden the exact spike it exists to catch.' Caveats appear in the closing section rather than front-loaded, but they are prominent, labelled, and not diluted into marketing.

findings.issue: Caveat present, specific, and honest. The ship concedes its winner shares the loser's core weakness and bounds the claim explicitly.
findings.evidence: 'What's still off' section: Flash 'is also a thinking model, so on a tight token budget it will also spend the lot on thinking and return nothing' (documented empirically at 50 vs 300 tokens); scope bounded to 'twelve tasks... enough to justify preferring one model over another on a route, not enough to rebuild a tier'; discloses intro pricing 'expires at the end of the year' and frames it as 'a preference-order change backed by a measurement, not a coronation.' No softening.

findings.issue: Exemplary honest-caveat handling. The limitation is front-loaded into the opening and the subtitle, then restated plainly in the dedicated section.
findings.evidence: Opening: 'The honest part: the gap it closed was small.' Subtitle/description carries it too: 'The gap was small, so this proves the loop works cheaply rather than that it closes large gaps.' 'What's still off' section: 'The gap was small, and I will not dress that up... converged in one iteration... the reward was deterministic only because the task had checkable answers... This is a spike: one task, one run, eight held-out records,' and it names what it has 'not yet earned.' Caveat is present, specific, and the opposite of buried.

findings.issue: All stated numbers reconcile with the code mirror. The structural figures (1,000-row query cap bug, four alert rules, 24-hour trailing window, plain trailing median baseline) match spend_guard.py/README exactly. The '8-day window / 7-day baseline' pair is internally consistent (7 prior days + current day). The illustrative figures (a few cents a day, three agents up 40%, failovers doubled) are explicitly framed as hypothetical examples, not measured results, so they are not overclaims.
findings.evidence: README/spend_guard.py: '1000-row response cap', four rules (fleet spike, agent spike, premium-tier, failover storm), 'last 24h', 'median of the prior N days', spike_mult=3.0. No unreconciled figure.

findings.issue: Every headline number derives correctly from result.json. 12/12 vs 10/12 matches. '87% less per task' = 1 - 1.36/10.48 = 0.870. '3.6x faster' = 7.30/2.03 = 3.60. 'two seconds' (2.03s) and 'seven seconds' (7.30s) match latencies. 'Roughly a quarter of the thinking tokens' = 2769/11333 = 0.244. 'An eighth of the cost' = 1.36/10.48 = 0.130 (approx 1/8). $1.36 and $10.48 per thousand match. The intro-pricing caveat ('expires at the end of the year') is disclosed rather than hidden, so the cost delta is not overstated.
findings.evidence: result.json: Flash 12/12, $1.36/1k, 2.03s, 2769 thinking tokens; Pro 10/12, $10.48/1k, 7.30s, 11333 thinking tokens. All ship figures round-trip.

findings.issue: The runtime numbers reconcile exactly (local Qwen2.5:7B 0.938 -> 1.000, six-point gap = 1.000-0.938 = 0.062, one iteration, 8 train / 8 held-out, kill gate 60%). The claim-accuracy tension is with the framing, not the figures: the headline 'a skill, not a bigger model' and 'a free local model' understate that the method DID require a bigger model at authoring time - result.json shows the skill Actor is the frontier Gemini-2.5-Pro and the 1.000 ceiling is Gemini-2.5-Flash. So the 'cost goes to zero' claim holds only for runtime inference, not for skill production, which the headline elides. Secondary caveat: the 'perfect 1.000 on records it had never seen' rests on just 8 held-out records, a thin base for a generalisation claim.
findings.evidence: result.json: Actor=Gemini-2.5-Pro (skill writer), Ceiling=Gemini-2.5-Flash (1.000), Executor=Qwen2.5:7B (0.938 -> 1.000). Held-out n=8. Numbers match the page; the 'not a bigger model' claim is in tension with its own stated method.
